newsitem.title: USA: Jesse Jackson seeks meeting with R.R. Donnelley.
newsitem.headline: Jesse Jackson seeks meeting with R.R. Donnelley.

text.p: Civil rights leader Jesse Jackson is seeking a meeting with executives of R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co, which faces a $500 million racial discrimination lawsuit brought by former Donnelley employees.
"We're planning for a Monday or Tuesday meeting," said Stephanie Gadlin, a spokeswoman for the Rainbow PUSH Action Network, a civil rights organization headed by Jackson.
R.R. Donnelley spokesman William Lowe said the company had not received an official request for a meeting.
"We have not been contacted officially," Lowe said. "Officially, we are closed today."

R.R. Donnelley has denied charges in the suit, which alleges that the world's largest commercial printer discriminated against black employees when arranging transfers in 1993 related to a plant closing. R.R. Donnelley said Tuesday it was "outraged" at what it called "inflammatory accusations and characterization of the company."

Jackson met earlier this month with the chief executive of Texaco Inc over a racial discrimination suit filed by six black employees in 1994. Jackson and other civil rights leaders called for a national boycott of Texaco. Texaco recently agreed to a $176 million settlement to the suit.
